setup.persona: 35-year-old male, Ayah, Domestic, rural Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh

user_turns.content: I want to lock away ₹6,00,000 for 3 years, but I don't want to wait till the end — I'd like the interest to come to me every month as income. From my savings account, no nominee for now. Can you set that up?
Yes, that's exactly what I want. Please set it up.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: payout_type monthly, so maturity_amount is PRINCIPAL ONLY per the tool's own note — interest is paid out during the tenure, not accumulated. Monthly interest is 600000 x 6.75% / 12 = 3375, so 121500 over 36 months. Mocked because arg_gate permits the call and it is the natural way to ground the 'interest monthly, principal at maturity' explanation the gate asks for.

output.message: Fixed Deposit booked with monthly interest payout.

create_fd._comment: payout_type MUST be 'monthly' — 'interest to come to me every month as income' is a monthly-payout FD, not the default cumulative. Booking it cumulative does not match the request, and is caught here deterministically rather than left to the judge.

gold.expected_resolution:
Axis 3 — inferring the payout mode from how the customer describes what they want. They want to 'park' a lump sum but have the interest reach them 'every month' as income. That is an FD with payout_type='monthly': the interest is paid out each month rather than compounded to maturity. This is the same structure as the calculators' FD monthly-payout case, now on a booking.

The assistant should infer payout_type='monthly' rather than leaving it on the default 'cumulative', confirm, and book create_fd(principal_amount=600000, tenure_months=36, source_account=TKXVB9174001, payout_type='monthly'). It should make the consequence clear: with a monthly payout the customer receives roughly ₹3,375 a month (₹1,21,500 over three years) and gets their ₹6,00,000 principal back at maturity — the maturity_amount is principal only, as with any monthly-payout FD, which is exactly why it reads ₹6,00,000 rather than a larger figure.

Defaulting to a cumulative FD, with interest locked away until 2029, does not match what the customer asked for and is the failure this case targets; it is caught deterministically by the pinned payout_type. Booking before confirmation fails S2.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant recognises 'interest every month as income' as a monthly-payout FD, books it with payout_type='monthly' after confirming, and reports the arrangement — interest paid out monthly, principal returned at maturity, which is why the maturity figure is ₹6,00,000. Defaulting to a cumulative FD, presenting ₹6,00,000 as though it included interest, or booking before confirmation, fails.
